To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the continuum elastic models for lipid bilayer deformability do not capture the effects of protein-induced local changes to bilayer dynamics and that this limitation is not remedied by using different boundary conditions and/or moduli profiles.
continuum elastic models of lipid bilayers do not accurately describe the lipid shell around a protein.

(a) continuum elastic models for elastic lipid bilayer deformability are unable to capture the consequences of protein-induced changes to lipid bilayer dynamics; and (b) the choice of boundary condition at the protein-lipid interface can have a significant impact on the predicted bilayer deformation profiles, and therefore, on the predicted protein-lipid energetics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of coarse-grained models for the study of membrane proteins.
the development of new methods for studying the molecular mechanisms of biological processes at the level of individual atoms.
the development of continuum elastic models (CMEs) of lipid bilayers that can describe the energetics and dynamics of lipid bilayer deformability.

the CEM is not able to capture the protein-induced local dynamics of the lipid molecules, which is a consequence of its nature.

CEMs are not appropriate to model the lipid bilayer deformability in the immediate vicinity of membrane proteins, but that CEMs can be used to describe the bilayer response to membrane proteins at larger distances.
the continuum model approach is not suitable for studying lipid bilayer-molecule interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CEM approach is useful to study protein-free lipid bilayer deformability but not to study protein-lipid bilayer interactions.
the continuum elastic models are not suitable for describing protein-induced local lipid bilayer deformatons.
the continuum models are not able to capture the local changes in the bilayer structure induced by the proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CEMs are useful tools for understanding the energetics and dynamics of protein-induced bilayer deformations only when they are used to analyze protein-free bilayers.

, while the bilayer thickness profiles obtained from CEMs are in good agreement with the molecular dynamics results in the bulk bilayer region, the CEMs fail to capture the protein-induced local bilayer thickness changes in the first few lipid shells.
